editorial:
You follow Jacob Moore, a young Wall Street trader whose mentor dies after a rival ruins their firm. With the economy shaking, Jacob teams up with Gordon Gekko, the famous former raider who just got out of prison. Gekko wants back into the game and also wants to fix things with his daughter, who happens to be Jacob's fiancée. The movie mixes money talk, family drama, and revenge, so it feels like a glossy thriller with a serious edge. You get big offices, fast deals, and tense meetings, but the heart is Jacob trying to do the right thing while everyone around him chases profit.

Michael Douglas is fun to watch as Gekko, and Shia LaBeouf carries the emotional side well. The pacing is steady, though some finance scenes can feel long if you are not into stocks. The pros are strong acting, a slick look, and timely story about greed. The cons are a few heavy speeches and a plot that sometimes gets crowded. If you like crime dramas with real-world stakes, this is a good pick. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final stretch, Gekko helps Jacob expose Bretton James and secure money for Jacob's green energy project. He also makes peace with Winnie as she prepares to have a baby. But the twist is that Gekko secretly takes $100 million from a Swiss account Jacob helped him reach and uses it to launch his own hedge fund. The last scene shows Gekko at the hospital for his grandchild's birth, then checking stock prices on his phone, hinting that his old greed is still alive.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves crime dramas with real-world stakes.
